narrative.overview:
The whole surface is one continuous sheet of tabulating paper lying on a grey-green desk. A form manufacturer printed the pre-print in form green: field names, ruled boxes, column heads, section rules, tick boxes, the tear-off reply slip. A dot-matrix printer then struck the data onto it in ribbon black. Red on the same ribbon appears only where something is reversed or a rule fires. Every element belongs to one of those three inks, and the question "who put this on the paper, the form or the printer?" decides its face, size and colour.

Density is that of a payslip: compact boxes with hairline shared rules, figures in fixed-character columns, totals bottom right. Rank never comes from type size on the printed layer; it comes from capitals, double strike and red. The sheet is broken into sheets by fanfold perforation, not by cards or panels. It is light only, because it is paper.

Motion is the print head: printed text reveals left to right in hard steps, once on load and again when a line is reprinted, and not at all under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Three inks: form green pre-print, ribbon black print, ribbon red for reversals and violations.
One printed type size (17px Doto 900) for every figure, list and message the printer produces.
Tractor holes and micro-perforation as background layers of the paper itself; fanfold perforation between sheets.
Hairline grids built from 1px gaps over a green ground, never from boxed cards.
A single solid button per reply slip; everything else is a printed link or an underlined pre-print text button.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Every mark is pre-print green, ribbon black or ribbon red. A fourth hue does not exist on this paper.

rules.name: The Red Fires Rule
rules.body: Red appears only when a rule fires or an entry is reversed. If nothing is wrong, the screen has no red.

rules.name: The Printer's Links Rule
rules.body: Links inside printed text are ribbon black with an underline; green links belong to pre-printed or typed prose.

rules.name: The One Druckgrad Rule
rules.body: The printer has one size (--druckgrad) and one line height. Printed hierarchy comes from capitals, double strike (text-shadow 0.05em of currentColor) and red, never from a larger size.

rules.name: The Who Printed It Rule
rules.body: If the form manufacturer would have printed it, it is Fira Sans Condensed in green. If the printer would, it is Doto in black. Typed correspondence is Fira Sans.

rules.name: The Ink Not Lift Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the paper casts a shadow. Separation is a rule, a hairline grid or a tint band.

dos: Do decide every element's ink by asking whether the form or the printer put it there.
Do keep all printed text at --druckgrad (1.0625rem) with a 1.5rem line; rank with capitals, double strike or red.
Do separate content with 2px green section rules, hairline grids and fanfold perforations.
Do align printed columns in ch of the print face on a shared grid template.
Do keep the print-head reveal stepped, once per print, and off under reduced motion.
donts: Don't use red for anything but reversals, violations and errors.
Don't enlarge printed text to make a figure important.
Don't add rounded cards, drop shadows on content, or a dark theme; it is paper.
Don't add a second solid button to a slip or a solid button outside a slip.
Don't introduce a fourth hue or gradients beyond the paper's own layers (tractor holes, perforation, fanfold crease, letter ruling).
